newsitem.title: ITALY: Iran's foreign minister says Italy a key partner.
newsitem.headline: Iran's foreign minister says Italy a key partner.

text.p: Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati said on Wednesday that Iran and Italy were interested in closer relations.

Velayati, ending a two-day visit for talks with Italian leaders and at the Vatican, told reporters at Rome airport that Italy could be one of Iran's most important commercial, economic and political partners.
"For that reason, we are ready to deepen and improve our bilateral relations," Velayati said.

"From the discussions I have had with Italian authorities, it was clear that Rome wants to have closer relations with us," he said, adding that Italy recognised Iran as playing a key role in the Gulf, Middle East and Central Asia.
Velayati met Prime Minister Romano Prodi on Wednesday.
He also met his Italian counterpart Lamberto Dini on Tuesday evening and had talks at the Vatican with Secretary of State Cardinal Angelo Sodano.

"During the course of the meeting, they reviewed relations between the Vatican and Iran, in particular the issue of freedom of the various religions present in Iran," Vatican spokesman Joaquin Navarro-Valls said.
He said Velayati and Sodano also exchanged views on the problems of the Middle East peace process.
The Italian Foreign Ministry said on Tuesday that Dini told Velayati he hoped Iran would increasingly distance itself from what he called international terrorism.
Dini also said Italy intended to continue along the route of "critical dialogue" begun by the European Union "to favour the gradual reintegration of (Iran) in international relations".
Europe's position contrasts with that of the United States.

Washington has urged the international community to isolate Iran, contending that it sponsors terrorism and plays host to Islamic fundamentalists bent on destabilising governments in North Africa and the Middle East.
Velayati's reception was criticised by the opposition National Resistance Council of Iran, which is linked to the Iraq-based Mujahideen Khalq armed opposition group.
